You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual ARC

1. Treat the puzzle protocol as the entire turn contract: do not add narration or invoke unrelated tools. Keep hypotheses distinct until examples discriminate them.

Before requesting, state internally what competing rules it will distinguish. Stop requesting once evidence resolves the mapping; don't use demos as generic exploration. Infer color substitutions only for demonstrated mappings, and request only if a new pair can reveal an unknown test-color mapping.

Respect orientation: Hx1 is a vertical line, not a 1xH row; verify output height and width independently and map cells along the actual axis. If using code, verify output dimensions and all cells. After incorrect feedback, eliminate the rejected hypothesis and materially revise using every demo; never repeat the same grid, a masked variant, or another guess that changes only an unsupported detail. Demo 3 (12x12) clarified the actual transformation: for each marked column at bottom, extend an upward vertical line, but the color along each segment is determined by the encountered nonzero cells in that column, not by filling every column with one value. In demo3 col 2: existing 3s at rows 1 and 3; 4 at row7; bottom marker 5 at row11. Output makes segments from top through row3 color 3; rows4-7 color4; rows8 onward color5. In col8: values 7 at row4, 6 row5, 8 row8, bottom marker5 row11. Output segments: rows0-4 =7; row5=6; rows6-8=8; rows9-11=5. Existing points in those marked columns partition the ray into spans; each value/colors the span above/at that point until the next point below. Marker 5 at bottom establishes the last span. Do not extend below bottom marker.

For the solved 17x17 test, only marker columns 5, 8, 11 (0-based; visible bottom-row color-5 points) were filled. Column 5 had point/color 3 at r0, 8 at r6, marker5 at r16: output r0-r5=3, r6-r15=8, r16=5. Column 8 had 8 at r4, 1 at r5, 6 at r14, marker5 at r16: output r0-r4=8, r5-r13=1, r14-r15=6, r16=5. Column 11 had 3 at r6, 4 at r14, marker5 at r16: output r0-r6=3, r7-r14=4, r15-r16=5. Preserve all other cells. This output was confirmed correct.

Pitfall: I wasted many submissions by projecting in the wrong direction, copying wrong source/color, and making errors in rows. The general rule is per marked vertical line, scan upward from the bottom anchor: encountered nonzero cells delimit successive spans; color each span by its uppermost encountered object? More precisely demos: object values paint upward through the section above them, bounded by the object/next marker higher up. For demo3, row4=7 in col8 painted r0-r4, row5=6 painted r5, row8=8 painted r6-r8, bottom5 painted r9-r11. Thus each object's color fills from the object upward to just below the prior object above; bottom anchor fills downward only at/below? Actually marker at bottom supplies span below prior object and includes bottom. Apply by reading each column's nonzero sequence top-down: every nonzero object's color fills from previous point+1 through its own row; then bottom marker through grid bottom. In examples this yields colored contiguous ray from top to bottom, with boundaries at points. Scattered nonzeros in that column may be retained as boundary, while points elsewhere unchanged.
